clue.text: Show pine's wrong in a bodega

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of order, so these words are to be rearranged

parts.note: pine is taken as written; the 's stands for 'is', a link joining fodder to indicator

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a display of pine wood in a Spanish bar has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' shuffles SHOW and PINE together into the answer; read 'pine's wrong' as 'pine is wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine bar or store, so it is a shop selling wine.

clue.text: A once-revered figure, as is written repeatedly

indicators.note: something written repeatedly appears more than once, so the little word is set down twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that a formerly worshipped figure appears exactly as the text shows, over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link here; only 'is' is written twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a goddess worshipped in ancient Egypt, a deity once revered but no longer.

clue.text: Run to raise money and totter

indicators.note: in a down answer the money symbol is raised, set on top of the other piece

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound (librum), the unit of British money
a totter is one who tots up figures, an adder

explanation.surface: A charity runner wobbles while trying to raise funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'totter' looks like wobbling but means someone who tots up sums. A run in tights is called a ladder in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a ladder is a run in stockings or tights, where threads come undone in a line.

clue.text: The man's filled up with endless biscuits — such a bloomer

indicators.note: a thing filled up with something has that stuff put inside it

parts.note: his is the possessive for 'the man's'

indicators.note: the word is cut short by losing its ending, the plural tail of three letters

parts.note: taken as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A man's tin crammed with broken biscuits leads to an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips the plural tail -its from the word, and the stub fills up the man's HI_S. 'bloomer' means a mistake on the surface but here a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hibiscus is a shrub grown for its large showy flowers, so it is literally something that blooms.

clue.text: One English monarch who didn't rule the waves

definitions.text: One English monarch who didn't rule the waves

parts.words: One English monarch who didn't rule the waves
parts.note: the legend of the king who sat on the shore and ordered the tide back, which ignored him; a twist on the song lyric 'Britannia rules the waves'

explanation.definitionFit: Legend says this eleventh-century king of England commanded the tide to halt and it did not obey him.

clue.text: Working steadily, or quietly taking a rest

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction meaning quietly
someone taking a rest may be lying down

explanation.surface: A choice between someone working hard or quietly having a lie-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply a trade is to work at it steadily, so plying is working diligently.

clue.text: Remedial treatment, if dirt's a problem

indicators.note: a problem here means the letters are in a troubled state, to be sorted into new order

parts.note: taken as written
dirt and its S taken as letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Treatment applied when dirt in a wound is causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate care given to an injured person, treatment that remedies before a doctor arrives.

clue.text: Clothes may be spared

indicators.note: the letters may be something else, a hint that they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that some garments might be saved from the clear-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' reads as a noun but is the verb, to dress or cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To drape something is to cover it loosely in fabric, so drapes means clothes in the verb sense.

clue.text: Very cold? It depends

parts.note: something very cold that 'depends' in the old sense of hangs down, from eaves or gutters

explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is frozen water hanging from a ledge, cold and literally pendent.

clue.text: They'll fix the drinks

definitions.meaning: pins or ... hold things in place, such as tent ropes or washing
a peg is a measure of spirits, a drink, in older British and Indian usage

explanation.definitionFit: Pegs fasten things; and a peg is also a tot of spirits.

clue.text: Way back, flying coppers in with security equipment

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way
on the wing, awing, means flying
p, pence, copper coins in British money
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police officers speeding back down the road with security gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RD into DR; 'coppers' are pennies, not police. The security is the hold a pin gives a sheet of paper on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawing pin secures paper to a board, so it is a small piece of fastening equipment.

clue.text: Search ordered by an engraver

indicators.note: putting letters in order means arranging them afresh

explanation.surface: A police search instigated by a craftsman who engraves metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaser is a craftsman who decorates metal by chasing, engraving or embossing its surface.

clue.text: Good man with top position

parts.note: St, saint, is the crossword's good man
and means together with
a point is a tip or top

explanation.surface: A good man holds the highest office.
explanation.definitionFit: A standpoint is the position from which one views a matter, an attitude or point of view.

clue.text: Being out of ready money, barter

parts.note: ex means out of or from, as in ex-works
change is coins, the cash in hand

explanation.surface: Someone who has run out of cash has to trade goods instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange is to trade one thing for another, which is what bartering is.

clue.text: Force receiving a tribute

indicators.note: a word receiving another takes it inside

parts.note: to prise is to force something open with a lever

explanation.surface: The police force are given a commendation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts A inside PRISE. 'Force' suggests police, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is commendation, the kind of approval that a tribute expresses.

clue.text: Flag that is quite normal

definitions.meaning: a banner carried on a pole

explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner or flag, and standard also means normal or typical.

clue.text: One's to prosecute ringleader — he's put out

parts.note: one is I, and the 's is added to it
to sue is to take legal action against
the leader, or first letter, of the word ring

explanation.surface: Someone means to prosecute the head of a gang who has been ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' means the first letter of 'ring', R. 'put out' is to be read as issued, not upset.
explanation.definitionFit: An issuer is one who issues something, putting out stamps, shares or statements.

clue.text: Soldiers authorised to appropriate a vehicle — and appropriate's the word for it!

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

indicators.note: to appropriate is to take something in, so the vehicle goes inside

parts.note: let means allowed or authorised
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Troops cleared to commandeer a lorry, and the setter remarks on how fitting the word is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' appears twice: first as the containment signal, then as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevant means pertinent or suited to the matter, much as appropriate does.

clue.text: Sea bed made lower

indicators.note: these letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: The seabed was dredged and so lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase is to lower in quality, value or character.

clue.text: Plant discovered by island circumnavigator

parts.note: the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea
Sir Francis Drake sailed round the world in the sixteenth century

explanation.surface: A plant discovered on an island by a famous explorer who sailed around the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a plant of the nightshade family with a forked root, famed in folklore.

clue.text: A gold-plated key — antique

indicators.note: gold plated over the key would cover it, so the key letter goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An old gold-plated key described as an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plated' puts E inside GOLD; 'key' is the musical sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Age-old means very old, of long standing, as antiques are.

clue.text: Announces the end in ringing tones

definitions.text: Announces the end in ringing tones

parts.words: Announces the end in ringing tones
parts.note: the slow tolling of a bell at a death or funeral

explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the sound of a bell rung solemnly for a death, so tolls of it mark an ending.

clue.text: Had youngsters fooled

definitions.meaning: a goat that gives birth is said to kid

explanation.definitionFit: A goat kidded when it bore young; and to kid someone is to fool them.

clue.text: Support an employee when old

parts.note: to second is to back up or support a proposal
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Someone backs a member of staff when they are elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods are used, previously owned, and so old rather than new.

clue.text: Propose relocation

definitions.meaning: to ... a motion is to propose it formally
a change of house or place

explanation.definitionFit: One moves a motion at a meeting; and a move is a change of home.

clue.text: Tea when the game's over?

definitions.meaning: a South American herbal infusion made from yerba leaves
in chess, checkmate ends the game

explanation.definitionFit: Maté is a South American infused drink, and mate is the chess call that ends a game.

clue.text: Girl who's a little angel — inordinately good

indicators.note: only a little of these words is used, a run of letters sitting in them

explanation.surface: A girl who behaves like a little angel and is exceedingly good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes a run from angEL INORdinately.
explanation.definitionFit: Elinor is a girl's name, as for the elder Dashwood sister in Sense and Sensibility.

clue.text: Say round about a hundred can organise the putting up

indicators.note: one piece going round the others contains them

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means
re means about or concerning
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a tin with about a hundred items can sort out a construction job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the example abbreviation round three pieces. 'can' looks like a verb but is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Erecting is building or setting up, arranging for a structure to be put up.
